# FeatBit Provider

Terraform provider for managing FeatBit through its documented public REST API.

The provider manages Projects, Environments, Feature Flag definitions,
environment-specific Segments, custom Policies and their complete statement
sets, Groups, exact Group-Policy and Group-Member bindings, and one existing
Member's complete direct-Policy set. Exact single-object data sources observe
core objects, custom or built-in Policies, existing Groups, and existing
Members without adopting their lifecycle.

IAM ownership is deliberately narrow. Group bindings own one exact pair, not
a Group's complete relationship collection. The direct-Policy resource is
authoritative only for one Member's direct Policies and never changes inherited
Group Policies. Built-in Policies are read-only.

Member invitation, creation, profile changes, organization or workspace
removal, and deletion are unsupported. The provider can authenticate with an
existing personal or service access token, but it does not create Service
Tokens or assign them to Groups. Flag evaluation, deployments, analytics,
audit streams, Portal-private APIs, and generic raw REST access are also
outside this release.

Segment targeting writes do not create Environment End Users or register
custom End User Property metadata. The canonical Segment example uses the
built-in `keyId` property; direct targets and custom-property rules require
their Environment prerequisites to exist independently. IAM Policy statements
can authorize Segment operations, but they do not add those prerequisites.

For a hands-on workflow across Dev, Stage, and Prod, follow the
[FeatBit Terraform GitOps Tutorial](../GitOpsGettingStarted.md).
It complements this reference with an end-to-end Terraform root, idempotence
checks, promotion, cleanup, and explicit current capability boundaries.

For a hands-on IAM workflow, follow the
[FeatBit Terraform IAM GitOps Tutorial](../GitOpsGettingStartedIAM.md).
It covers custom Policies, Groups, direct and inherited Member access, scoped
Policy updates, association-safe deletion, and dependency-ordered cleanup.

## Authentication

Set `FEATBIT_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the provider process environment. FeatBit service
tokens created outside this provider are recommended for CI/CD. Service Token
lifecycle and Group assignment remain unsupported. Do not put access-token
values in Terraform configuration, variable defaults, committed environment
files, plans, state, or logs.

FeatBit Cloud is the default API origin. `FEATBIT_API_URL` can select another
documented `/api/v1` origin. A configurable origin does not certify an untested
self-hosted FeatBit version or deployment.

## API endpoint

No endpoint setting is required for FeatBit Cloud. To select another documented
public API root, configure `api_url` explicitly:

```hcl
provider "featbit" {
  api_url = "https://featbit.example.com/api/v1"
}
```

Alternatively, leave `api_url` unset and export the same URL through
`FEATBIT_API_URL`. The value must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host,
an optional port, and either no path or `/api/v1`; the provider normalizes both
forms to `/api/v1`. User information, query strings, fragments, and other paths
are rejected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.0.0"

  required_providers {
    featbit = {
      source  = "featbit/featbit"
      version = "= 0.2.0-beta.1"
    }
  }
}

# Set FEATBIT_ACCESS_TOKEN in the process environment. Keep token values out
# of Terraform configuration, variable defaults, plans, state, and logs.
provider "featbit" {
  # Omit api_url for FeatBit Cloud. For another documented public API root,
  # uncomment the next line or set FEATBIT_API_URL to the same form.
  # api_url = "https://featbit.example.com/api/v1"
}
```

The provider block deliberately leaves authentication to the process
environment. Optional timeout, concurrency, and read-retry settings can also
be supplied through the environment variables documented in the schema.

The first IAM release candidate is `v0.2.0-beta.1`. Terraform prereleases
require an explicit version selection, so this example deliberately pins the
exact beta for real-scenario validation. Review the release notes and update
the constraint and lock file deliberately for a later beta or stable
`v0.2.0`.

## Exact identity and Import

Data sources never select the first fuzzy search result. Project and Policy
keys and Group names are organization-scoped and case-sensitive. Environment
keys are case-sensitive within an exact Project. Member email lookup compares
the complete organization collection by case-insensitive full equality. Every
selector rejects zero or duplicate exact matches.

Managed resources retain these stable Import forms:

| Resource | Import ID |
|---|---|
| Project | `<project_uuid>` |
| Environment | `<project_uuid>/<environment_uuid>` |
| Feature Flag | `<environment_uuid>/<exact_key>` |
| Segment | `<environment_uuid>/<segment_uuid>` |
| Custom Policy | `<policy_uuid>` |
| Group | `<group_uuid>` |
| Group-Policy binding | `<group_uuid>/<policy_uuid>` |
| Group-Member binding | `<group_uuid>/<member_uuid>` |
| Member direct Policies | `<member_uuid>` |

Use child resource references for dependency ordering. Destroy Feature Flags
and Segments before their Environment, and destroy Environments before their
Project. Remove Group bindings before destroying their Group or a custom
Policy. Each resource page describes its replacement, ownership, and deletion
behavior.

## Schema

### Optional

- `access_token` (String, Sensitive) FeatBit personal or service API access token. May also be set with `FEATBIT_ACCESS_TOKEN`; service tokens are recommended for CI/CD.
- `api_url` (String) FeatBit API base URL. May also be set with `FEATBIT_API_URL`. Defaults to `https://app-api.featbit.co`. The path may be empty or `/api/v1`.
- `http_timeout_seconds` (Number) Timeout in seconds for one FeatBit HTTP request. May also be set with `FEATBIT_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Defaults to 30; valid range is 1 through 300.
- `max_concurrency` (Number) Maximum number of concurrent FeatBit API requests. May also be set with `FEATBIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`. Defaults to 4; valid range is 1 through 32.
- `max_retries` (Number) Maximum retry count for safely retryable reads. Mutations are never retried automatically. May also be set with `FEATBIT_MAX_RETRIES`. Defaults to 3; valid range is 0 through 10.
